propositions: The drain advisory lock is held across entire LLM call chains (437s and 131s observed), causing single-flight drain behavior and blocking concurrent drainers with lock-held skips.

Restructuring drain() into three phases (collect under lock -> enrich unlocked -> finalize unlocked) reduces lock hold from multi-minute to seconds, enabling 3 concurrent drainers with up to 20-item batches.
Stale-writeback revalidation in finalize phase detects ticket state changes between claim and emit, skipping the digest emit and re-enqueueing with soak 0 to prevent stale enrichments.
Lease-expiry recovery and concurrency-cap guard (max 3 distinct live-lease drainers) prevent duplicate processing and bound concurrent resource consumption.
Batch cap is raised from 5 to 20 and clamped to lease_ttl_s // 40 (~22 at 15-min default) to prevent lease expiry mid-batch and limit per-write LLM cost.

Throughput post-restructure scales from ~5 items per multi-minute exclusive lock to 3 concurrent drainers × 20-item batches with collect-only lock hold, draining the standing ~1,046-entry backlog through normal workflow traffic.
